title: JsnodeScriptReprojectionRule
description: The rule a JSNode script standardization run applies as data: which candidate scripts it is safe to re-project to the canonical one-export/JSDoc/import.meta.main NDJSON command form, which gates an actual re-projection must clear, and what happens on a gate failure. A kept re-projection also writes each data/records/schema/<command>.{input,output}.schema.json file the generator's files array names alongside the script, under the same gates. Consumed by apps/standardize-jsnode-scripts.mjs; never re-authored per run.

discoverer.description: The exact published operation@version that reads a script's source into a JsnodeOperationArguments record (readJsnodeOperationArguments).

generator.description: The exact published operation@version that projects a JsnodeOperationArguments record back into canonical source text (projectJsnodeOperationSourceFromArguments).

candidatePredicate.description: A script is a re-projection candidate exactly when every named field of its JsnodeScriptDiscoveryReadout row (or, for readsStdin, its own freshly-read JsnodeOperationArguments record) equals the value given here.

exportCount.description: readout row field exportCount must equal exactly 1: one exported function.

descriptionPresent.description: readout row field hasDescription must be true: the exported function carries a JSDoc description.

residueEmpty.description: readout row field residue (a count) must equal 0: no top-level declarations besides imports, the one export, and the main guard.

hasMainGuard.description: readout row field hasMainGuard must be true: a real import.meta.main command guard is present.

readsStdin.description: The freshly-read JsnodeOperationArguments.readsStdin must be true: the guard reads process.stdin, so canonical projection preserves the command's face.

gates.description: Ordered checks an actual re-projection (candidate text differs from its canonical projection) must clear before the projected bytes are kept.

onFailure.description: The one recovery action when any gate fails: restore the exact original bytes, never leave a partially-applied projection.
